title: Price Salience and Product Choice
authors: Tom Blake; Sarah Moshary; Kane Sweeney; Steven Tadelis
eligible_reason: Randomized field experiments on StubHub (2012 and August 2015 upfront vs back-end fee arms), not a staggered-adoption DiD. The headline estimates (Tables 2-3, 7, funnel, covariate balance) are produced by SQL on proprietary data and are not in the package. The shipped Stata regressions are: (i) percent_chosen.do, cross-sectional reg of choice percentile / purchase on the AIP arm dummy (2012 experiment); (ii) weekly_spending.do, reg total_spent treatment#week i.week on buyers who purchased during the 2015 experiment: arm-by-week interactions with a pooled arm dummy and no buyer FE; the arms differ only during the experiment window (BF arm switched Aug 19 2015, the rest of the site at the Sep 1 2015 rollout), so this is a two-arm experiment around a common start date, not staggered adoption; (iii) round_listings.do, log listings on position/round x post (single date Aug 31 2015) with date FE; (iv) googletrends.do, site x post (single date Sep 1 2015) for StubHub/Ticketmaster/SeatGeek with date FE. All post dates are common to every treated unit.
design_notes: Stata (reg, areg). Seven do-files in code_price_salience2/. Data are proprietary StubHub data; the package ships only simulated .dta/.xlsx files generated with runiform()/rnormal() that do not mimic the true moments (readme.txt). Remaining tables come from SQL code not included.
